target.title: fix(plugins): bound hosted catalog feed reads on non-streaming responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readHostedCatalogResponseText` in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.ts` used two read paths: the streaming branch incrementally enforced `maxBytes`, but the non-streaming branch called `response.text()` first and only checked the byte count afterward. That check-after-allocate pattern could OOM on oversized bodies when the response was not stream-backed or when `Content-Length` was missing or wrong.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route all hosted catalog feed reads through the shared `readResponseWithLimit` helper from `src/infra/http-body.ts`, reusing the same byte cap, idle timeout, and overflow error contract as other bounded HTTP reads. For stream-less fetch shapes, fail closed instead of trusting `Content-Length` before the shared helper's `arrayBuffer()` fallback. This deletes the duplicate streaming loop and the unsafe `response.text()` branch.

## User Impact

Normal hosted catalog loads are unchanged for stream-backed responses. Oversized feeds fail at the shared byte cap; stream-less feeds now fail closed with `hosted catalog feed streaming response body unavailable` instead of trusting `Content-Length` and risking a full-body allocation.

## Evidence

```bash
node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Non-streaming hosted catalog feed reads could allocate the full response body before enforcing `maxBytes`; stream-less oversized bodies could still buffer via `arrayBuffer()` fallback.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin), Node.js v22.22.0, `node:http` loopback server on `127.0.0.1`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs
  ok: unbounded read pulled the full oversized feed (1572963 bytes)
  ok: rejected oversized hosted catalog feed
  ok: bounded error message present
  ok: streamless hosted feed with underreported content-length is rejected
  ok: streamless hosted feed never reaches arrayBuffer()

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ rejects non-streaming hosted feeds before buffering underreported bodies
 ✓ rejects oversized streaming hosted feeds incrementally
 ✓ rejects non-streaming hosted feeds without content-length

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  55 passed (55)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `loadHostedOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEntries` rejects a ~1.5 MiB loopback feed at the 1 MiB cap with `hosted catalog feed exceeds 1048576 bytes`; stream-less responses are rejected with `hosted catalog feed streaming response body unavailable`; and the underreported `Content-Length` proof confirms that path never reaches `arrayBuffer()`.
- **What was not tested:** Live ClawHub hosted catalog endpoints; proof used loopback fetch and mocked `fetchImpl` only.

## Tests and validation

- `node --import tsx scripts/proof-hosted-catalog-bound.mjs` (committed on branch)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- Regression tests added in `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts`

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? Yes — oversized hosted feeds error at the cap on stream-backed responses; stream-less hosted feeds are now rejected.
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? Yes — hosted catalog feed reads now use one bounded HTTP reader and refuse stream-less remote responses.
- Highest-risk area: plugin catalog refresh / hosted feed fallback behavior on large but legitimate feeds.
- Mitigation: default cap remains 1 MiB; successful feeds are far below it; bundled fallback behavior is unchanged on overflow.

## AI-assisted disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
- [x] Human-run Real behavior proof from local setup

target.title: fix(runtime): reconcile stale running sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can leave a durable session row in `status="running"` after the underlying embedded run/task is already gone. In Telegram forum topics, that stale row makes the next message look like it is queued behind active work even when there is no live run to wait for, leaving the topic wedged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime already has several recovery paths for stuck sessions, restart recovery, abort handling, and delivery safety hooks, but they did not consistently reconcile persisted `running` session rows with the real active run/task registry. This PR adds a focused reconciliation path so rows that no longer have active work are closed instead of continuing to occupy a session lane.

## User Impact

- Telegram topics should recover when a previous run disappeared but the durable session row stayed `running`.
- `sessions.abort` no-active-run cases should not leave the session permanently wedged.
- Startup/stuck-session recovery gets a safer persisted-state cleanup path.
- The change targets stale runtime bookkeeping; it does not change model routing, command syntax, or Telegram delivery semantics beyond avoiding stuck lanes.

## Evidence

AI-assisted: yes. This came from local OpenClaw incident debugging where Hermes/Codex traced topic lanes stuck behind stale running rows.

Validation from the original PR branch:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.abort-agent-scope.test.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/agents/command/delivery.test.ts` — passed locally before PR creation
- `pnpm build` — passed locally before PR creation

Runtime evidence from the local rollout that motivated the fix:

- Telegram topic lane showed work ahead/active accounting even though no active run was present.
- Abort/recovery paths reported no active cancellable work while persisted state still blocked subsequent turns.
- After the reconciliation patch, stale running rows were cleared during recovery instead of leaving the topic wedged.

Known gap:

- The PR body originally used older `Summary` / `Root cause` / `Validation` headings. This update converts it to OpenClaw's current contributor format so the real-behavior-proof gate has durable authored problem/evidence sections.
